data.title: Lucid Offers $10,000 Credit in Canada, $15,000 U.S. Black Friday Deal
data.description:
Lucid is offering Canadian buyers up to C$10,000 in credits and 0% financing on select 2026 vehicles, while customers south of the border are getting a separate Black Friday deal on the updated 2027 Gravity Touring and Air Touring.

According to Lucid’s Canadian offers page, the 2026 Air Touring is listed at C$112,800, with buyers able to take advantage of a C$10,000 credit and 0% financing for up to 72 months through Lucid Financial Services.

The less expensive 2026 Air Pure is also eligible for 0% financing, along with a C$7,500 credit.

For those interested in an SUV, Lucid is offering up to C$10,000 toward a 2026 Gravity purchased with cash. Buyers who finance or lease instead can receive a C$7,500 credit, along with a 0.99% interest rate.

Lucid is also throwing in a C$4,000 allowance for qualifying trade-ins and a C$1,000 test-drive credit. However, the company’s Canadian website has conflicting terms for the test-drive offer, and may not be stackable with every other incentive.

These Canadian offers require qualifying deliveries by November 30, and the Lucid Credit does not apply to the 2027 Gravity.

Bigger Black Friday credits in the U.S.

Meanwhile, Lucid is offering American buyers even larger credits as part of a separate Black Friday promotion.

According to an early-access email sent customers this week, they can receive US$15,000 (C$21,272) toward a 2027 Gravity Touring or US$10,000 (C$14,181) toward a 2027 Air Touring. (via Reddit)

Both offers are US$5,000 (C$7,091) higher than the regular cash credits currently advertised on Lucid’s U.S. website.

There is a catch, however. The Black Friday credits are only available to customers purchasing with cash or third-party financing. Customers financing or leasing through Lucid Financial Services aren’t eligible.

The credits also can’t be combined with other incentives or discounts, and the promotion runs through November 30.

Incentives follow disappointing Q3 sales

The latest offers also come as Lucid tries to improve sales following a disappointing third quarter.

Lucid delivered just 3,806 vehicles during Q3 2026, down 4% from the previous quarter and 7% compared to the same period last year. The results also fell short of Wall Street expectations of 4,687 deliveries.

Production took an even bigger hit, falling 38% from Q2 to just 2,954 vehicles. However, much of that decline was intentional, with Lucid cutting production to reduce its inventory of unsold vehicles and improve cash flow.

data.title: Global EV Sales Return to Growth in October, Reaching 2.09 Million
data.description:
Global electric vehicle (EV) sales have returned to annual growth in October following a decline in September, with stronger demand in Europe and other markets helping offset weaker sales in China.

According to Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, global sales of battery-electric vehicles and plug-in hybrids reached 2.09 million units, up 8% year-over-year but down 3% from September.

Year-to-date sales reached 17.5 million vehicles, representing a 5% increase compared to the same period in 2025 (via Reuters).

Europe continued to lead growth among established EV markets, with sales increasing 36% year-over-year to 510,000 vehicles. Battery-electric sales climbed 49%, while plug-in hybrids rose 7%.

Meanwhile, North American EV sales increased 24% year-over-year to 130,000 units, marking the region’s first annual increase of 2026. However, the improvement reflects a weaker comparison period.

The U.S. federal EV tax credit expired in September 2025, leaving October as the first month compared against a period without the incentive.

China remained the largest EV market by far, recording 1.14 million sales despite a 12% annual decline. Sales nevertheless increased 5% compared to September.

Sales outside China, Europe and North America climbed 85% to 300,000 vehicles, exceeding North America’s total. Chinese passenger vehicle new energy vehicle exports reached almost 600,000 units in October, another monthly record.

data.title: Canada’s EV Market Share Climbs From 7% to 13% in 18 Months
data.description:
Canada’s electric vehicle (EV) market share, at 13% in August 2026, has nearly doubled from a year and a half earlier, after remaining virtually unchanged in the second quarter.

The new figures come from the Canadian Climate Institute, showing EV market share has climbed from a low of 7% in February 2025, following a sharp decline in sales caused by a rollback in government support.

Canada’s EV market continues to recover

The figures were released Thursday alongside the launch of the Climate Progress Tracker, a new interactive tool built by the Institute’s 440 Megatonnes project to monitor Canada’s transition to cleaner energy. The tracker measures EV market share using new battery-electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle sales as a percentage of all new light-duty vehicle sales.

A total of 22,716 new zero-emission vehicles were sold in August, representing 13.0% of the market, up from 8.8% a year earlier.

The recovery also follows the return of federal EV rebates in February 2026, offering buyers up to $5,000 toward eligible vehicles.

Clean energy and battery storage see strong growth

Beyond EV sales, the tracker uses more than 40 indicators across five categories: the clean economy, electrification, clean energy, industrial performance, and emissions progress.

Among its findings, Canada’s wind and solar capacity has increased by nearly 7 gigawatts since 2020, representing growth of more than 40%.

Battery storage capacity has also increased more than sixfold over the same period, reaching almost 900 megawatts in January 2026. Clean technology exports have grown to nearly 1.8 times their 2020 levels.

Canada still faces challenges meeting emissions targets

However, not every indicator is moving in the right direction. The share of electricity generated from non-emitting sources fell six percentage points between August 2020 and August 2026.

Meanwhile, emissions increased slightly in 2025 before declining slightly during the first half of 2026, leaving Canada well short of its climate targets.

data.title: Zoox Expands to Downtown Vegas and the Arts District
data.description:
Zoox announced that it is expanding its robotaxi service area from the Vegas Strip to include Downtown Las Vegas and the Arts District. The new service area also extends their service hours, with robotaxi rides running from 6 am to 3 am daily.

The extension comes 14 months after its initial launch in 2025 in the city. At launch, Zoox focused rides on and around the Vegas Strip as the first fully autonomous ride-hailing service using purpose-built vehicles.

The company has worked with several properties to organize dedicated and branded Zoox drop-off and pick-up zones, making it easier to find your next ride. This includes the Sphere, T-Mobile Arena, Resorts World, AREA15 and the Henry Reid International Airport.

Outside these specific pick-up areas, users will use the FindMyZoox feature in the Zoox app, which allows you to identify your ride in busy areas. Your Zoox ride will use sound cues and distinctive lighting to help you find the vehicle, and it will also provide licence plate information for easy identification.

With service also expanding in San Francisco and launches planned in Austin, Miami, Houston, and San Diego, Zoox is expanding methodically, and it seems to be working well for the company.

data.title: Tesla removes mid-tier Model Y AWD in U.S.
data.description:
Tesla has removed a version of the Model Y AWD from its U.S. order page. At the same time, delivery estimates for the remaining Premium trims slip have slipped further into 2027, much like Canada, although for different reasons..

Tesla first introduced the mid-tier Model Y AWD in February, priced at US$41,990, positioning it between the entry-level Rear-Wheel Drive at US$39,990 and the more expensive Premium models.

At just US$2,000 more than the base model, it offered buyers a relatively inexpensive way to get AWD without stepping up to the Premium trim. It even escaped Tesla’s May price increases, remaining at US$41,990 while the automaker raised prices on its Premium and Performance variants.

Now less than 10 months later, the trim has disappeared from the U.S. Design Studio.

Why did Tesla remove the Model Y AWD?

Tesla has not provided an explanation for its removal, but as with many of Tesla’s product decisions, it likely came down to demand.

Buyers looking for the cheapest Model Y likely chose the Rear-Wheel Drive (RWD), while those willing to spend more preferred to make the jump to the Premium AWD.

With the Premium AWD offering a more upscale configuration, the mid-tier AWD may have found itself in an awkward position between customers focused on price and those looking for additional features.

With its removal, the U.S. lineup now starts with the Rear-Wheel Drive at US$39,990, followed by the Premium Rear-Wheel Drive at US$45,990 and Premium AWD at US$49,990. Then there is the Model Y Performance AWD at US$57,990 and the larger Model Y L Launch Series at US$61,990.

Model Y delivery estimates pushed further into 2027

Along with the removal of the AWD trim, Tesla has also pushed back estimated delivery dates for several remaining Model Y configurations.

According to Tesla’s Design Studio, all Model Y Premium trims are now showing estimated deliveries between January and March 2027, compared to December 2026 through January 2027 previously.

The Model Y L has also seen estimated deliveries fall back, now stretching from February through April 2027, instead of January through March.

data.title: Tesla launches Supercharger for Business in Mexico and Colombia
data.description:
Tesla has launched Supercharger for Business in Mexico and Colombia, so businesses in both countries can buy and install their own Superchargers.

According to a Thursday LinkedIn post from Livio Caputo of Tesla’s Charging for Business team, the program is now live in both markets.

“Supercharger for Business is now live in Colombia and Mexico,” Caputo said.

Mexico and Colombia are the program’s first Latin American markets and bring Supercharger for Business to 37 countries. (via EVwire)

Tesla’s Mexican and Colombian program pages say businesses must buy a minimum of four Supercharger posts. They can hire their preferred installer, with a Tesla Design Engineer available to guide the process.

Hosts can monitor utilization, adjust pricing and track finances through Tesla’s portal, while Tesla handles servicing the equipment.

The white-labelled stalls come with the same hardware, software, pricing controls and service as Tesla’s own network, and can charge all compatible electric vehicles (EVs). They include idle alerts and real-time availability, and can appear on Tesla’s in-car map and trip planner.

The stalls also receive over-the-air (OTA) software updates for their full service life, and drivers can use their preferred charging app and payment method.

The program launched in Canada in October, along with Semi Charging for Business.

Tesla says it guarantees 97% uptime through a full service package that includes network operations, preventive maintenance and driver assistance.

data.title: Tesla Model Y delivery estimates in Canada slip to May 2027
data.description:
Tesla has pushed Model Y delivery estimates in Canada further into 2027, with new orders now showing estimated delivery windows stretching into as far as May of next year.

According to a review of the Canadian Design Studio by Drive Tesla, estimated delivery dates now show as March 2027 to May 2027, compared to January 2027 to March 2027 earlier this week.

The updated timeline applies to all new Model Y orders in Canada, regardless of which configuration customers select.

What is causing the longer delivery estimates?

Although Tesla has not provided an explanation for the extended wait times, one possible explanation is increased demand for the Model Y after Tesla stopped accepting new Model 3 orders in Canada due to the country’s Chinese EV import quota. With the Model 3 no longer available to order, some buyers may have turned to the Model Y instead, putting additional pressure on supply.

Unlike the Model 3, which is imported from Giga Shanghai in China, the Canadian Model Y is built at Giga Berlin in Germany. Despite Giga Berlin recently reaching a production milestone of 7,000 Model Ys in a single week, the factory supplies more than 30 markets worldwide, meaning Canadian orders are competing for production capacity with customers across Europe and other regions.

A combination of stronger Canadian demand and limited production capacity allocated to Canada could help explain why delivery estimates have now stretched into May 2027.

Model Y wait times continue to grow

While that may be the reason, this is the latest in a series of increases to Model Y delivery estimates in Canada, which have been steadily moving further into 2027.

Back in July, Tesla was already showing December 2026 delivery estimates for the All-Wheel Drive, while the Rear-Wheel Drive and Performance were showing December 2026 to January 2027.

By late August, delivery estimates had shifted again, with all three Canadian Model Y variants showing December 2026 to January 2027.

Canadian pricing and lineup remain unchanged

While delivery estimates have extended well into 2027, Tesla has made no changes to Canadian Model Y pricing – the Rear-Wheel Drive continues to start at $49,990, while the Premium All-Wheel Drive is priced at $64,990 and the Performance starts at $74,990.

The available lineup hasn’t changed either, unlike in the U.S. which saw a Model Y AWD trim disappear on Thursday night.

Unfortunately the Model Y L remains unavailable in Canada, as Giga Berlin does not yet produce the six-seat variant of the electric SUV.

data.title: Volkswagen Starts ID. Tiguan Production in Germany Ahead of 2027 Deliveries
data.description:
Volkswagen has started series production of the all-electric ID. Tiguan SUV at its Emden plant in Germany, marking another milestone ahead of the model’s arrival at dealerships in early 2027.

According to Volkswagen’s official announcement, the first production vehicle, finished in Olive Bronze Metallic, rolled off the assembly line in Hall 20b on Thursday.

Production Underway Ahead of 2027 Deliveries

The ID. Tiguan will replace the ID.4 and ID.5 in Volkswagen’s EV lineup. The automaker has already received several thousand pre-orders since the SUV’s premiere in early October.

Volkswagen confirmed that the Emden facility will gradually increase production over the coming weeks, with the first customer deliveries expected at the beginning of 2027.

Three Powertrain Options and Up to 600 km of Range

The electric SUV will be offered with three powertrain options, including rear-wheel-drive versions producing 140 kW and 210 kW, alongside a 220 kW 4MOTION all-wheel-drive variant.

Battery options include 58 kWh and 77 kWh packs, offering up to 600 kilometres of WLTP range depending on configuration. Maximum towing capacity reaches 2,000 kg.

Inside, the ID. Tiguan features a 15-inch central touchscreen, a 10-inch driver display, and an optional 12-inch passenger display, the latter being a first for a European Volkswagen.

Emden Continues to Expand EV Production

Volkswagen CEO Thomas Schäfer described the production milestone as an important step in the company’s EV strategy, which has delivered more than two million ID. family vehicles worldwide since 2019.

As part of that, Emden continues producing the ID.7, which was Germany’s most registered EV in October. The factory has produced more than 500,000 EVs to date.

data.title: Canada proposes higher luxury tax threshold for EVs
data.description:
The Canadian government has announced plans to raise the federal luxury tax threshold for fully electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles from $100,000 to $150,000.

According to the Department of Finance Canada, Finance Minister François-Philippe Champagne announced the proposal on Thursday, with the higher threshold taking effect on Friday, subject to subsequent parliamentary approval.

The change applies specifically to fully electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles. Gasoline-powered vehicles and other vehicles not covered by the proposal will remain subject to the existing $100,000 threshold.

How the new luxury tax threshold works

Canada’s federal luxury tax currently applies to qualifying passenger vehicles valued above $100,000. The tax is calculated as the lesser of 10% of the vehicle’s full taxable value or 20% of the amount exceeding the threshold.

Under the proposal, the calculation remains the same, but the higher $150,000 threshold would apply to eligible zero-emission vehicles.

What the changes mean for Tesla buyers

For Tesla buyers, however, the change will have little impact following the automaker’s decision to discontinue the Model S and Model X earlier this year. The Cybertruck, meanwhile, presents a unique situation due to its existing luxury tax exemption, as production of the electric pickup also nears its end.

The Cybertruck Premium AWD was last listed at $139,990 before Tesla stopped accepting new orders. The Cyberbeast remained available at $167,990.

If the federal luxury tax applied to those starting prices, the proposed change would reduce the Premium AWD’s tax from $7,998 to zero, while the Cyberbeast’s tax would fall from $13,598 to $3,598.

The government says the proposal is meant to reflect the higher starting prices of zero-emission vehicles.
